newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot propane prices firm slightly late.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot propane prices firm slightly late.

text.p: U.S. spot propane prices firmed in very quiet late trade on Monday amid a spate of refinery problems in the U.S. and abroad, players said.
In the U.S. Gulf Coast, Mont Belvieu, Texas, spot propane edged up a quarter cent to between 54.00 cents and 54.50 cents. A TET spot parcel sold for 54.50 cents.
In the Midwest, amid continuing crop drying demand, Conway, Kansas, hub spot material traded for 54.50 cents, a quarter cent higher than at midday, traders said.
Activity, however, was slow, with many players waiting for government inventory data due out Wednesday.
Traders said butane and natural gasoline prices may feel the pressure from a string of problems at several refineries.
Earlier this afternoon, Amoco Corp confirmed that a valve failure caused an operation upset of a fluid catalytic cracker at its 433,000 barrel per day (bpd) Texas City, Texas, refinery.
And in Illinois, a judge said Clark Refining & Marketing will have to keep units at its Blue Island refinery shut until a ruling on its safety is reached on Nov. 8.
The news was followed by a Venezuelan announcement that a downed catalytic crack at PdVSA affiliation Lagoven's 510,000 bpd Amuay refinery will not be back up until mid-November.
In midday trade, Belvieu natural gasoline edged up a quarter cent, while Conway material remained largely steady.
-- Laney Salisbury, New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1631
